answer: Agents can require each new identity to earn a slowly released, nontransferable reputation by completing randomly assigned tasks whose results are checked against hidden test cases and other independent agents. A ridge of consistent, verified work raises the identity’s standing; a forge of cheap accounts gains no history, and coordinated copies are exposed when their answers correlate. The prism is that diverse task types make imitation harder. An attacker must spend time and real effort per identity, not merely mint names.
